body: I like the idea a lot but in your example it would be favorable to take all of the parent nodes and their siblings into the account instead because then you won't need to add them explicitly. This probably needs a proposal to discuss more specific cases where baking with influence from parent nodes won't be enough

this is a really fantastic idea. I've had to just have a scene containing the directional light that I can place in the hierarchy of each lightmap. This seems very useful!

Wondering if this already makes it possible to include other objects? For instance I might have a lightmap for the terrain, and a seperate lightmap for each "town" or group of buildings on that terrain. Does this mean it would be possible to add the landscape to the "additional_nodes" of the town lightmap and get the bounce lighting off the ground into the town lightmap? If so that would be wonderful. Been wanting a way to have objects contribute indirect lighting or shadowing without having to be part of the lightmap for a while now.
I need this and I was thinking to create a proposal for this. Very good

Unfortunately no. Technically you can add any node hierarchy to `additional_nodes` and both lights and meshes will be fed into the lightmapper. However, every mesh can have only one lightmap assigned so whichever LightmapGI gets baked last, gets to overwrite previous lightmap assignment on that mesh. See [#8311](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8311) proposal regarding layered lightmaps. It's relevant to your use case.

So:
* Lights: Can be freely referenced by multiple LightmapGI nodes 
* Meshes: Can still be safely added to `additional_nodes` in a **single** LightmapGI instance.

Layered lightmaps also seems useful. But I think I probably didn't explain myself too well 😅

I don't mean that the extra objects added to `additional_nodes` would be assigned to the lightmap, just wondered if they would be fed in as an influence for the objects that ARE in the lightmap.

So back to my example. I have little towns that can pop up according to the timeline of an interactive map. The landscape is baked on one lightmapGI node and doesn't ever need to change. It's only influenced by the single lightmap (no use of layers needed right now) The towns have their own lightmap and also a little patch of ground for the purposes of building and contact shadows.

The only issue with this is if say, a mountain puts a town in shadow. Then I'd need to make a proxy of the landscape and make it a sibling of the town lightmap, but with a very low lightmap Texel density so as to not waste lightmap space, bake the lightmap, and then hide the proxy mesh.

 I just wondered if under this system if I added the main landscape as an additional node to a town lightmap if the shadowing and bounce of the main landscape would be taken into account WITHOUT affecting the main landscape in any way (it has it's own lightmap)

In other words, can we now add objects as an influence to a lightmap without actually affecting or baking the data of those objects? (for use as fake shadow casters, emissive meshes that don't need to have any lighting data since they're blown out, invisible bounce cards, etc)

I don't think that would break the requirement of each mesh only being affected by a single lightmap node, but would be extremely useful

Thanks for opening a pull request :slightly_smiling_face: 

Feature pull requests should be associated to a *feature proposal* to justify the need for implementing the feature in Godot core. Please open a proposal on the [Godot proposals](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals) repository (and link to this pull request in the proposal's body).

This feature seems to solve an issue that I’ve been facing in my project in the current 4.5 version.

In my project, I have levels constructed from multiple connected sections (scenes) that are loaded at runtime.
I had difficulties baking lights and shadows caused by another scene, but this feature (additional_nodes) allowed me to easily bake light sources and shadows (I tested it by fetching the pull request).

Is this going to be a feature in the Godot core?
I am worrying a bit, as @Calinou stated it should be opened as a proposal, but when I tried to look for it using the Godot proposal viewer, I could not find it and started worrying that this good feature might be left behind and forgotten.
However, I might be wrong about this, as I have no real experience with open-source projects on GitHub.
This is salvageable. @w4zdev open a proposal about this and maybe I can work it further if changes are needed
